item.title: Masuk girls volleyball pushes past East Lyme, wins first CIAC title in five-set thriller
item.description: Masuk's Grace Morrow (2) cries tears of happiness as she celebrates with teammate Mia Tyler (5) following their 3-2 win over East Lyme to capture the the Class L volleyball state championship Friday, November 20, 2026 at Bulkeley High School in Hartford. (Jim Shannon/Hearst Connecticut Media) HARTFORD - The third-seeded Masuk girls volleyball team went from a two-set lead to a fifth-set, winner-take-all battle in the CIAC Class L state championship match against top-seeded East Lyme on Friday night. The Panthers, who fell behind by three points early in that fifth set, dug deep, came back and dethroned the defending champion Vikings, 3-2, to win their first state championship. The set scores were 25-21, 25-20, 24-26, 27-29, 15-10. Senior captain Mia Tyler, who won MVP honors when Masuk captured its first South-West Conference championship earlier this month, was named Class L's most outstanding player. The Panthers finished 24-2 while the Vikings ended their season at 20-5. East Lyme held a 21-19 lead in the first set, but Masuk scored the final six points to strike first. Panther senior Jacqueline Silkman had a key tip during that run to give her team a 22-21 lead. Another tip by senior captain Grace Morrow ended the set in Masuk's favor. The second set was much the same as East Lyme ran out to an early lead, only to see Masuk come back ayet again. The Panthers finally caught up at 16-16, then the set was even again at 18-18 before the No. 3 seed made their push. At 24-20, Masuk, an East Lyme hit was out long to give the Panthers a 2-0 lead in the match. East Lyme ran out to an 8-3 lead in the third set, but stayed in control this time until Masuk caught them at 12-12. Trailing 15-14, Viking senior Natalie Knowlton scored six straight points, including five kills, for a 20-15 lead for the No. 1 seed. The Panthers came back to tie the set, 24-24, on a kill by junior Grace Kehoe. East Lyme senior Bella Albert had a block to put her team up 25-24, then sophomore Emma Knowlton's serve was not returned for a 26-24 set victory. The Vikings had hope, but the Panthers almost put them away in a frantic fourth set. Masuk owned two six-point leads, 14-8 and 21-15, but East Lyme ripped off six straight points to tie the set, 21-21, the last point coming on a Emma Knowlton kill. The Panthers took a 23-21 lead, only to watch the Vikings score three straight points to earn a set point at 24-23. An East Lyme hitting error and a Masuk ace by freshman Skylar Tengeres gave her team a match point, 25-24. A 31-second point went in favor of the Vikings on an Emma Knowlton kill to tie the set, 25-25. East Lyme senior Savannah Marusov served an ace for a 26-25 lead, but a net violation call tied the set again, 26-26. A Viking block made it 27-26, but Panther senior captain Addison Scott rocketed a hit through blockers to tie it again, 27-27. item.title: 5 takeaways from Oregon Ducks stylish 45-7 blowout over Michigan State
item.description: It was a game that the Oregon Ducks needed to win, and needed to look good doing so. They did just that. Dan Lanning's team got its first ever victory in East Lansing on Friday night, beating the Michigan State Spartans 45-7 in a game that really was ugly early on, but dominated in the second half. Spurred on by a fake field goal that went for a touchdown right before the break, Oregon scored 35 points over the final 30 minutes and seven seconds of the game, and put up some style points in the eyes of the College Football Playoff committee, which may have been the most important outcome of it all. The defense was dominant once again, while true freshman running back Brandon Smith stepped in for an injured Dierre Hill and had a coming-out party. Now, with a full day of college football ahead of us on Saturday, we will sit back and see how things unfold for the Ducks . Before that, though, here are our biggest takeaways from the game: Style Points Coming into this game, there was a notion that winning wasn't going to be enough for Oregon; the Ducks needed to win with style. Sitting on the outside of the College Football Playoff field looking in, an impressive showing was needed in order to help convince the committee that Oregon is playing as one of the best 12 teams in the nation right now, and deserving of a shot at the national championship. I think they accomplished that. It didn't look pretty for much of the first two quarters, with Oregon putting up only 166 yards and 10 points before a gutsy fake field goal at the end of the half. But over the final 30 minutes and seven seconds of football, the Ducks were dominant. They ended up with 422 total yards and 45 points, letting some of their most dynamic players — mainly RB Brandon Smith and WR Dakorien Moore — show what they could do while the defense was dominant once again. A lot of things can happen in order to clear the Ducks' path to the playoffs, and we may see some of them come to fruition on Saturday, but even if some upsets don't take place, there's a reason to believe that Oregon might be able to get in at 9-3. Games like this one certainly help build the case. The Brandon Smith Game Without Dierre Hill for a majority of this game (more on that later), this quickly turned into the Brandon Smith game for the Ducks. Oregon fans knew before this game that they had something special in the true freshman, but he cemented that fact in this one, rushing 14 times for 121 yards and two touchdowns. It wasn't just the stats, but the way that he ran, shifting through contact, maintaining elite balance, and dancing down the sideline on impressive big gains. He looked good enough to get legendary Oregon RB Jonathan Stewart to make this statement: "Brandon Smith the best back in a Oregon jersey since Kenjon Barner." — @Jonathanstewar1 https://t.co/lxrIEzV7QT — Zachary Neel (@zacharycneel) November 21, 2026 Whether you agree with Stewart or not is beside the point. It's impossible to deny at this point

item.title: Instant Recap: Michigan State gets stomped by Oregon
item.description: Michigan State’s Derrick Simmons, left, tackles Oregon’s Da'Jaun Riggs during the first quarter on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026 in East Lansing. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Whew, boy. That was the worst loss of the season. It was all Oregon tonight. Michigan State’s offense struggled early, and Oregon scored halfway through the first quarter to give the Ducks a 7-0 lead behind a Brandon Smith 5-yard touchdown run. Frederick Moore had a nice one-handed snag right before the second quarter started, but Liam Boyd would miss a 47-yard field goal for Michigan State’s first chance to put points on the board. The offense was starting to look solid behind Kayd Coffman’s play, but he would trip while running out of the pocket to turn the ball over on a 4th-and-3 from Oregon’s 28-yard line. The defense did their best to keep the Spartans close, but their special teams did not. Chrishon McCray would muff the next punt by the Ducks to allow Oregon to take over in the redzone. The defense held tough and forced them to kick a field goal, and it made it a 10-0 game. Near the end of the first half, Dan Lanning called a fake field goal where the Ducks’ kicker was able to run it in from 15 yards out to give Oregon a 17-0 lead heading into halftime. Once that fake field goal scored, it felt like the game was already out of reach. Oregon opened up the second half with another touchdown run, this time from Simeon Price, to put them up 24-0. Michigan State would respond with a touchdown of their own with a direct snap from the 1-yard line by Jaz Patterson, though it would be the only points they scored all night. Both Brandon Smith and Simeon Price would add another touchdown run each for the Ducks, and Dylan Raiola found Dakorien Moore for a nice one-handed touchdown pass as Oregon continued to pile on the points. Oregon would go on to win 45 to 7. Michigan State moves to 3-8 Kayd Coffman completed 10 of his 19 passes for 106 yards and one interception. Jaz Patterson handled 16 carries, but only managed 26 yards. Brandon Tullis added 25 yards on eight carries. The Spartans’ leading receiver was Fredrick Moore with 31 yards on two catches. It was a brutal loss, and one of those games where you wish it could’ve ended by the end of the third quarter, as Oregon kept putting more and more points on the scoreboard. Luckily for the Spartans, it’s not the end of the season, and they’ll finish it off with a matchup at Rutgers on Thanksgiving weekend. Let’s hope they can finish the season with a win. Go Green!

item.title: Couch: 3 quick takes on Michigan State football's 45-7 loss to Oregon
item.description: MSU battles as best it can against Oregon. That won't be acceptable against Rutgers. EAST LANSING — There are levels to this sport. And Oregon is on a different level than Michigan State right now. To MSU’s credit, the gap wasn’t as severe for parts of the night as it looked like it might be out of the gate, or as it appeared at the end on the scoreboard. I don’t know what does for MSU at this point, knowing you hung in there for a while and landed a few blows of your own in a 45-7 loss. It’s something to take into next week and into the offseason as you evaluate the roster, I guess. The Spartans ’ defense is playing some good football at times. MSU’s offense had some moments of life with young Kayd Coffman under center. For it to mean anything, they’ve got to beat Rutgers, the wet basement of the Big Ten. There are no moral victories next week in Piscataway. MSU wore down Friday night. The Spartans looked like a pesky Mid-American Conference team, with a few playmakers who belonged on the stage, playing a Big Ten team, with too much talent and depth. It’s a story as old as time. It’s just getting old that it’s sometimes MSU on the other end of these games. Oregon is fighting for a place in the College Football Playoff, a three-loss team that needs to impress a committee that appears to be in bed in the SEC. Hence the deep passes with a 38-7 lead. MSU is now an eight-loss team, trying to keep its chin up all the way to the finish line. If the Spartans’ special teams — their strength all season — hadn’t played their worst game by a mile, this final score might have been more indicative of the actual chasm between the programs, something like 31-10. That’s not exactly heartwarming. But that’s what this game was essentially — a 31-10 home loss to a program that’s where the Spartans want to be in terms for resources and year-over-year winning. And November stakes. This game was, at the very least, instructive. For this MSU season, next week is a bigger deal. You can’t lose three straight to close the season, including at Rutgers, and feel good going into a massive offseason, even with the win over Michigan. You’ve got to get one more W, and show that you’re not in the same realm as Rutgers. 2. Coffman shows improvement from his last start There is no question that freshman Kayd Coffman has some ability. You can see the lively arm and good feet. He’s at his best right now when they roll him outside of the pocket. item.title: MSU hockey falls at Michigan, suspensions coming after 3rd-period brawl
item.description: Lansing State Journal sports reporter Nathaniel Bott breaks down No. 9 Michigan State's 5-1 loss to No. 1 Michigan on Friday, Nov. 20 at Yost Ice Arena in Ann Arbor. What happened MSU came into Friday night looking to rebound after a two-point weekend at Notre Dame, facing off with rival Michigan for the only time in Ann Arbor this year, at least for the regular season. THE BIG PICTURE: MSU hockey looks to jump-start season with rivalry test against No. 1 Michigan The Spartans got off to a slow start, allowing a goal in the first six minutes while the Wolverines registered the first 11 shots on target. U-M would make it 2-0 on a goal from freshman forward J.P. Hurlbert (a 2026 Detroit Red Wings draft pick) with just over eight minutes remaining in the first period to bring the crowd back alive. The Spartans would get one back in the dying moments of the first period, with freshman Jack Hextall winning an offensive zone face-off back to freshman defenseman Tommy Bleyl, who then fed the puck down low back to Hextall, who delivered a pass through the U-M crease. Forward Cullen Potter, who shifted to the wing for the first time this season Friday, was there to jam the puck past goaltender Jack Ivankovic with just 21 seconds left in the first period to give the Spartans some momentum. MSU carried that into the second period, outshooting U-M 16-6 with multiple solid chances, but Ivankovic stood firm. U-M would later get a 3-on-1 rush the other way, and defenseman Asher Barnett beat MSU goaltender Joshua Ravensbergen to restore U-M's two-goal lead. The Wolverines would score twice more early in the third period, and then the fireworks began. MSU sophomore defenseman Sean Barnhill laid a big hit on U-M forward Nick Moldenhauer at the Michigan blue line, sparking a big scrum with Barnhill getting a two-minute minor for boarding and each side receiving matching roughing calls. With things seemingly settled down, MSU senior defenseman Patrick Geary went over to the U-M bench, sparking a number of Wolverine players to react and prompted all three MSU players to leave the penalty box and start the brawl again. Fireworks in the third period, Michigan up 5-1 and havoc at the bench pic.twitter.com/kyr0EvrgV1 — Max Bultman (@m_bultman) November 21, 2026 This time, however, the officials handed out multiple fighting majors, which carry a minimum one-game suspension. In total, U-M's Drew Schock, Michael Hage and Nic Sima, as well as MSU's Barnhill, forward Shane Vansaghi and defenseman Matt Lahey all received that penalty and will be suspended for Saturday's game, at minimum. Additional discipline could be handed out by the Big Ten after reviewing the incident. Ravensbergen made 33 saves for the Spartans, who fall to 6-4-1 on the season. Ivankovic stopped 37 MSU shots, as the Wolverines improve to 11-1. item.title: Jaguars score early, shut out nationally ranked Sals for soccer title
item.description: FREDERICA – Appoquinimink scored just four minutes into the DIAA Division I Boys Soccer Tournament final. In a sport where goals are rare and very difficult to get, it was a sweet and satisfying start. It also meant perennial powerhouse Salesianum, ranked 15 th in the nation, had the added incentive to score and 86 minutes in which to do it. The Sals could not, and Appoquinimink won a state championship that will long be as cherished and coveted as such accomplishments can be Nov. 20 at DE Turf. Freshman Caiden Stone scored that fourth-minute goal and the Jaguars spent the rest of the game thwarting one Salesianum opportunity after another, including two in the final minute alone. “It was just everybody,” senior captain and center back Gabriel Arbuet said. “Everybody worked their tails off. Last game of the season. Seniors especially, last game of their careers. “We just worked hard the whole entire time. We knew what was on the line. We knew we could make history. It was a whole team effort.” Third-seeded Appoquinimink (16-1) was playing in its sixth state boys soccer championship game, all since 2013, every one against Salesianum. The Jaguars prevailed in only one of those, the 2020 final on a tie-breaking penalty-kick shootout, which was their last title-game appearance. “We had a game plan going into it,” Appo coach Lance Berry said. “We worked on it the past two days and the boys executed perfectly. “So hats off to Sallies. They're a hell of a program. They're the standard. But our boys showed up tonight. Really proud of each and every guy.” Top-seeded Salesianum (15-3), its national ranking courtesy of the United Soccer Coaches, had beaten Appo 2-1 on Oct. 22. But both teams had conceded afterward that, with Appo missing three starters that night, a rematch might be even more competitive. It most certainly was, especially with the determination Salesianum gained with that early deficit. But the Sals, who’d won 20 of the last 24 state soccer titles and were appearing in their 17 th straight title game, couldn’t level the match despite numerous opportunities. Sometimes, perhaps out of a sense of desperation, they may have unleashed shots too early and from too far away rather than working for something better. Berry was happy to point out that the Jaguars set a school record with their 13 th shutout, having won all three state tournament games 1-0. They allowed five goals all year. “The defense has been lights out all year,” said Berry. “To be honest with you, I'm not too surprised . . . When we had all of our guys healthy, they have given up maybe a goal when they're all on the field.” Berry has now won boys and girls state titles as coach at both his alma mater Caravel and Appo. He again joined his dad John, who steered McKean to the 1984 title and was in attendance, on the list of championship coaches. item.title: Raines denied in Jacksonville's first-ever Open Division football game
item.description: JACKSONVILLE | He trudged through Duval County mud and across the goal lines adjacent to Moncrief Road to history four times, and Brian Wilson Jr. couldn't remember the last night that felt anything like that. "Maybe Little League?" the Miami Columbus running back guessed. The first-ever Florida High School Athletic Association Open Division game ever played within Jacksonville city limits was a winner for Wilson. But not for the home crowd, or the hometown champions. Watch Florida high school playoffs live on NFHS Network Got a great play? How to submit your high school sports highlights to the Times-Union Fueled on offense by Wilson's four touchdowns, and stifling the reigning state champions from start to finish, Miami Columbus closed the door on Raines' Open Division hopes and downed the Vikings 28-6 on Nov. 20 at the Graveyard. For the first time in six years, the 2025 state champion Vikings (10-2) have lost consecutive games, after going down 28-7 at West Boca Raton on Nov. 13 in the round-robin Open Division format. A gritty effort from a depleted Raines defense wasn't enough against the Explorers (11-1), who frustrated the Vikings throughout a night of wind-driven tropical downpours. But to end in the win column, Columbus needed the four scores from Wilson, the sophomore power back splitting carries with Northern Illinois-bound senior Cecil Smith. "After four touchdowns," Wilson said, "I feel amazing right now." MISCUES DERAIL RAINES' HOPES After sophomore Sa'Mon Ellison-Morgan took a 15-yard quarterback keeper up the middle with 4:30 remaining in the first quarter, tying the score 6-6, Raines seemed ready to match the state's second-ranked squad highlight for highlight. It didn't turn out that way. The Columbus defensive front seven, highlighted by Chanavis Chance Jr., Tyler Tindal and Damien Harvey, plugged the rushing lanes and harassed Ellison-Morgan (2 for 13, 6 yards) all night. Harvey, the 265-pound nose tackle, recovered a fumble and picked off a pass off a Tindal tip. item.title: Berlin football holds off Middletown, clinches its 5th straight playoff berth
item.description: Berlin's Gamaliel Ayizano, 4, tries to push his way past Middletown's Juel Ocasio, 54, during the CIAC football game between Middletown and Berlin high schools.Friday, November 20, 2026, Sage Park, Berlin, Conn. (H John Voorhees III/Hearst Connecticut Media) BERLIN - The Berlin Redcoats are in. If there's any justice in the football world, the Middletown Blue Dragons will also qualify for the postseason, because on Friday night at Sage Park both teams showed they belong there. In a Central Connecticut Conference game played six nights before Thanksgiving, but befitting the playoff stage that will follow the holiday, Berlin clipped Middletown 35-32 to beat its neighbor to the south and qualify for the CIAC tournament for a fifth straight year. This baby was by far the closest of the five. What appeared to be a TKO when Berlin scored on the third play of the game and then recovered a fumble on Middletown's first snap instead turned into a 15-rounder that wasn't over until Berlin junior wide receiver Anthony Frayler secured an onside kick with 37 seconds left. Both teams scored five touchdowns. Both teams finished 7-3. The difference lay in Berlin junior Noah Foster going 5-for-5 on extra points and Berlin's defense stopping Middletown on all but one 2-point conversion try. A 31-yard touchdown run by Foster, coming with 1:56 left out of Berlin's new-wrinkle Wildcat, proved to be the game-winning score. Middletown, which had hung tough behind touchdown jaunts of 75, 15 and 60 yards by junior running back Nick Cyril, answered that Foster score to keep hope alive. Junior QB Matteo Fletcher, coming on early in the second half when starter Brendin Smith went down with an injury, hit senior Sebastiano Bibisi with a 38-yard pass on a fourth-and-10, then rifled a 12-yard TD pass over the middle to senior Victor Bonet. Berlin stuffed the 2-point run, then recovered the ensuing onside. And with that, last year's Class M state champ clinched a berth in the Class SS playoffs. Middletown remains in the top eight in Class MM at 7-3 and will secure a berth if any of the 6-3 teams on its heels - Fairfield Prep, Platt and Torrington - lose their regular-season finale next week. Even if all three win, Middletown might still get in on bonus points. On Friday night, the Redcoats drew opening blood on a 43-yard TD run by junior Brandon Sadowski on toss-right out of the double-wing. Also for Berlin, senior running back Gamaliel Ayizano broke off a 62-yard scoring dash straight up the middle, Frayler corralled a 30-yard TD pass down the right sideline from junior QB Chace Hrubiec and junior RB Nick Balicki muscled in a crucial score late in the first half on fourth down from the 1 after Middletown had made three stops inside the 3. The Blue Dragons got on the board via a 60-yard pick-six from Bibisi. Foster and Sadowski had interceptions for Berlin. Junior Liam DeSantos had the fumble recovery on Middletown's first snap. item.title: Darian DeVries wants the Indiana-Kentucky rivalry series to continue
item.description: Nov 20, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indiana Hoosiers head coach Darian DeVries looks for an intentional foul against the Kentucky Wildcats during the second half at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A lot has changed from when Indiana and Kentucky agreed to resume their longstanding annual rivalry series in men’s basketball. Darian DeVries took over as head coach for the Hoosiers ahead of the first matchup in the 2025-26 season, which was Mark Pope’s second year as the head coach of the Wildcats. Neither was in their position when the series was agreed upon, with Mike Woodson and John Calipari leading their respective programs at the time. Resuming the series was a priority for Woodson, who took a game at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis rather than Assembly Hall in Bloomington to get it done. Now it’s DeVries’ program and he, like Woodson before him, wants the Wildcats on future schedules. DeVries, coming off of a 90-76 win over Kentucky in that very game in Indianapolis on Friday night, was asked if he’d like the series to continue in the future, beyond its current four-game slate. “I would love to keep it going,” DeVries said. “I think it’s great for college basketball and it’s fun games for everybody. The fanbases, proximity, to have two historic programs like this continue to play non-conference… yeah. item.description: EAST LANSING – Depleted at quarterback. Banged-up at running back. Out of bodies at linebacker. All of the injuries finally caught up to Michigan State football . And there was nothing the Spartans could do – no matter how hard they competed and fought through them – to stop No. 14 Oregon. The Ducks started slow, thanks in part to another staunch defensive showing early by MSU before losing Brady Pretzlaff early in the first half and fellow linebacker Dion Crawford early in the third quarter. Kayd Coffman started his second game this season, and the true freshman finished 10-for-19 for 106 yards and an interception. Quarterback Dylan Raiola went 21-for-34 for 234 yards with a touchdown for Oregon (8-3, 6-2), but 103 of his yards (including his 31-yard TD pass to Dakorien Moore) came in the fourth quarter after the Ducks entered the final period with a 24-point lead.. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team.
